confirmed.statement: S1 recruited 78 fifth-grade students from three classes in eastern China; the reported 42 boys and 36 girls sum to 78 people. The reported ages are 10?12 years (M = 11, SD = 0.51).

The paper explicitly states random assignment to GenAI-supported writing (20 students), peer-collaborative writing (38 students; 19 pairs), and individual writing (20 students), supporting all three arm n_randomized values and the total of 78.

confirmed.locator: PDF p. 7, Table 1, N column; p. 5, Figure 1, collection of all participants? handwritten samples for analysis.

confirmed.statement: Writing self-efficacy and flow analyses also report N = 20, 38, and 20, so these outcomes do not introduce smaller or additional participant samples.

confirmed.statement: S1 alone meets criterion 2 with 78 analyzed people across all three randomized arms. The GenAI-versus-individual comparison contains 40 people, but the codebook applies the threshold across all study arms.

summary: The source supports 78 people randomized and analyzed in S1: 20 with GenAI, 38 in 19 peer pairs, and 20 writing individually. No participant-count error was found, and S1 meets the 50-person threshold; peer-score dependence and cross-paper overlap remain unresolved.
